messages:
lina: quick notes from today's smoke: tried a 'bridge-prefetch-lite' mode on LlamaY-13B-q8 for quant bring-up. shaved latency but saw a small EM dip on a hand-curated QA set. jotting things down before the holdout sweep.

oscar: please include commands + configs so we can reproduce on the smoke pool.

lina: will do. run used: ./eval/run_local.sh --model LlamaY-13B-q8 --mode bridge-prefetch-lite --cfg configs/bridge_lite.yaml --seed 7 --dataset eval/hand_qas.jsonl --batch 4 --output /tmp/bridge_lite_1787777000.json

lina: perf summary (baseline = no-bridge-lite -> bridge-prefetch-lite): p50 52ms -> 33ms (~1.58x), p95 240ms -> 150ms (~1.60x), tokens/s 110 -> 170 (+54%). host GPU mem steady, CPU spin negligible.

tyler: interesting. does the win hold for longer contexts?

lina: synthetic 2k stream: per-token 9.0ms -> 6.8ms (~1.32x). improvement attenuates as KV cache fills.

oscar: quality metrics? any regression on exact-match or Rouge?

lina: hand_qas exact-match: baseline 78.6% -> bridge-lite 78.1% (-0.5pt). BLEU/ROUGE within noise. Did a 100-sample human triage: ~65 rephrases, ~20 benign alt-answer, ~15 true regressions (shortening that dropped a crucial clause).

lina: sample regression (prompt removed):
--- baseline: "The certification requires that all components pass the thermal coupling test before integration."
+++ bridge-lite: "Certification requires components pass the thermal test before integration."
(comment: dropped "coupling" which matters in some cases)

qa-bot: qa-check started for job id br-1787777000; storing artifacts in s3://redwood-ci/bridge-lite/br-1787777000.tar.gz

oscar: hypothesize causes: 1) quantization noise interacts with approximate softmax used during bridge prefill, 2) prefetch path uses a shorter-precision logits path for speed, nudging low-prob tokens downward. we should log top-k ranks for initial tokens to verify.

lina: did that - logged top-10 ranks for first 20 tokens on 50 cases. median rank-shift per-token ~1.2 positions; median KL per-token ~0.0038. differences concentrated at tails.

tyler: run A/B on lookahead param? default 10 here?

lina: yes default lookahead 10. queued lookahead 6 vs 10 vs 14 on same seed 7. expecting more regressions at lookahead 6.

lina: config snippet: 
# configs/bridge_lite.yaml
strategy: bridge-prefetch-lite
bridge:
  lookahead: 10
  softmax_mode: approx_fast
  confidence_cutoff: 0.88
fallback: quant-rollback
quant: q8
batching:
  dynamic: true
  max_batch_tokens: 8192

oscar: important to test quant-rollback behavior: if rollback occurs often we'll lose tail latency benefits. add metric for rollback-rate per 1000 requests.

tyler: agree. also add KL-drift and exact-match delta to alerting. limit initial rollout to session routes under 10 tokens median.

lina: scheduled a 10k-sample holdout for seeds [7, 73, 211] across datasets: MMLU-subset, hand_qas, regen-surge. aim: p95 latency, EM delta, rollback-rate.

infra-bot: job br-1787777000 completed: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/bridge-lite/br-1787777000.tar.gz; perf report at /reports/bridge-lite/br-1787777000.html

lina: preliminary notes from the artifact: rollback-rate 1.8% overall, higher (~3.5%) on regen-surge prompts. KL drift higher on long answers but not huge. looking into whether we can restrict bridge-lite to short-turn routes.

oscar: if rollback concentrates on regen-surge, we might route those to full-precision or use higher lookahead specifically for that route. per-route config is useful.

tyler: SRE comment: watch multi-tenant Dedicated nodes for increased variance; prefill lite adds an extra CPU precompute step that showed occasional 10-20ms spikes on cold workers in previous experiments.

lina: noted. I'll add cold-start probe to the smoke harness and an infra flag to disable bridge-lite on nodes with CPU load > 70%.

lina: next steps: 1) finish A/B lookahead sweep and post diffs to /shared/br_lite/1787777000/, 2) run full 10k holdout with seeds above, 3) produce short onboarding note for devex highlighting rollback-rate, lookahead defaults, and per-route gating.

oscar: I'll take the diff triage (borderline regressions). tyler will coordinate rollout with SRE.

tyler: will do. schedule a 20-min sync tomorrow to decide canary percentage and per-route gating.

lina: thanks all. will post a calendar invite and upload the summary doc when the A/B finishes. :sparkles:
